name: Make a Square
description: You are given a positive integer $$$n$$$, written without leading zeroes (for example, the number 04 is incorrect). In one operation you can delete any digit of the given integer so that the result remains a positive integer without leading zeros. Determine the minimum number of operations that you need to consistently apply to the given integer $$$n$$$ to make from it the square of some positive integer or report that it is impossible. An integer $$$x$$$ is the square of some positive integer if and only if $$$x=y^2$$$ for some positive integer $$$y$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^{9}$$$). The number is given without leading zeroes.
output_specification: If it is impossible to make the square of some positive integer from $$$n$$$, print -1 . In the other case, print the minimal number of operations required to do it.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.
